description: The National Flood Hazard Layer is FEMA's national compilation of digital flood hazard mapping for the United States. The public NFHL map service (version 2.9.0, NAD83 geographic coordinates) exposes 32 layers, including flood hazard zones, base flood elevations, levees, cross-sections, coastal transects and Letters of Map Revision. It is produced and maintained by FEMA. The data are available free through the FEMA Flood Map Service Center, which offers NFHL downloads by state and by county, and through the public ArcGIS REST map service; no licence is named on the pages read, and as US federal data it is generally free to reuse. Caveats: the layer shows mapped flood zones and elevations only where digital mapping is effective, not depth grids or future climate conditions, and map currency varies by county. It is the standard flood exposure layer for overlaying US infrastructure assets in hazard exposure and resilience analyses; a related record is the FEMA National Risk Index, which summarises risk by county and tract.
